title: LabIDEAS: Impact-Driven Education for Action and Sustainability
description: The IDEAS Lab develops educational models and design-based interventions aimed at advancing sustainability and social responsibility in higher education. Grounded in human-centered and impact-driven pedagogies, it integrates research, teaching, and community engagement to promote the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through design. The project explores how educational ecosystems can generate social innovation and ethical awareness, combining methods from design, psychology, and learning sciences.
notes: DFH Activity Plan 2025–2029 (Project 2).

title: ICDC: International Creative Design Challenge
description: The International Creative Design Challenge (ICDC) is a transnational initiative connecting design students, educators, and institutions through collaborative creative challenges. Anchored in empathy, diversity, and intercultural understanding, it fosters cross-disciplinary collaboration between universities and promotes design as a driver for positive social change. It produces educational and scientific outcomes including exhibitions, publications, and case studies that explore creativity as a form of global citizenship.
notes: DFH Activity Plan 2025–2029 (Project 3).

title: PUSH: Project – Ubiquitous Success for Humanity
description: The PUSH project is an internally funded research initiative that aims to establish an academic model integrating design, technology, communication, psychology, and the social sciences to foster human development through inter-, multi- and transdisciplinary collaboration. Grounded in design research and pedagogy, it connects scientific innovation with applied teaching practices, aligning its activities with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It promotes active learning and design methodologies such as Challenge-Based Learning and Problem-Based Learning to address real-world challenges in diversity, mental health, and sustainability, producing outputs such as community partnerships, publications, and curricular integration.
notes: DFH Activity Plan 2025–2029 (Project 1).

title: Collecting and Conserving Digital Art in Portugal
description: The purpose of the project Collecting and Conserving Digital Art in Portugal is to contribute to the creation of a model for the conservation of Internet-based digital art in Portugal. It aims to ensure the longevity of the country's recent technocultural and artistic past, addressing the contradiction between rapid innovation cycles and the short lifespan of current technologies versus the need for durable conservation of born-digital artworks. With no existing conservation model in Portugal that meets the requirements of this kind of art, the project proposes to develop a Model for the Conservation of Internet-Based Digital Art in Portugal through an in-depth study of the conceptual, artistic, and technological situation of online digital artworks created in Portugal and analysis of strategies and measures for preservation. Key research questions include: What is the status quo of online artworks created by artists in Portugal? What kind of conservation model for Internet-based digital art is needed in the country?
notes: MADx Activity Plan 2025–2029.

title: Designing Phygital Experiences and Business Models
description: This research investigates the convergence of physical and digital experiences—“phygital”—to enhance customer engagement and brand interaction. It explores immersive technologies, service design, and user experience strategies to create seamless, meaningful touchpoints across channels. The project also examines how phygital models can drive innovation in retail, education, and cultural sectors.

title: Building Design and Innovation Capabilities
description: Focused on organizational transformation, this project aims to embed strategic design capabilities within companies and institutions. It includes tailored interventions such as design audits, capability-building workshops, and co-creation sessions. The goal is to foster a culture of innovation and empower teams to solve problems creatively and sustainably.

title: Supporting Open Innovation with Gamification
description: This initiative leverages gamification to foster open innovation ecosystems. It connects startups, corporates, and academia through playful, challenge-based formats that encourage idea generation and rapid prototyping. The project includes the development of gamified platforms, innovation sprints, and collaborative design games to stimulate engagement and creativity.

title: Humanizing the Digital Transition
description: Digital transformation often lacks emotional resonance. This project focuses on integrating emotional design and digital empathy into digital systems and services. It aims to make technology more inclusive, intuitive, and human-centered, particularly in sectors like healthcare, education, and public services. Methods include persona development, empathy mapping, and affective interface design.

title: Tackling Innovation Challenges through Industry–Academia Collaboration
description: This project explores how gamified and design-driven methodologies can be used to address complex innovation challenges in collaboration with industry partners. It promotes autonomous, interdisciplinary teams composed of students, researchers, and professionals from various sectors. The approach emphasizes early-stage ideation, stakeholder engagement, and iterative prototyping, reducing risk and enhancing the quality of innovation outcomes.

title: Entrepreneurship Brokering Network
description: This project aims to bridge the gap between innovative ideas and capable teams by creating a brokering network for entrepreneurship. It includes mentoring programs, matchmaking platforms, and gamified collaboration formats to support early-stage ventures. The initiative is particularly relevant for incubators, accelerators, and university-based innovation hubs.

title: Through the Looking Glass: A dive into the microcosmos
description: This interdisciplinary workshop invites students to playfully explore the unseen beauty of the microscopic world as a source of inspiration for their creative works. Through hands-on sessions using microscopes to observe biological samples, students collect images, translate these visuals into design concepts, and develop projects ranging from artworks to conceptual designs or three-dimensional models at diﬀerent scales.

title: Mycelium-Based Packaging (sustainable material + design management framework)
description: The project aims to develop a durable, biodegradable packaging material using mycelium, possibly in combination with other organic or recycled components, that can withstand shipping conditions while minimizing ecological impact. In parallel, the research will propose a design management model, outlining how such a solution can be developed, implemented, and scaled within a small to medium-sized enterprise (SME) environment.
notes: BID Activity Plan (Dec 2022).

title: INVASIFI: Invasive Alien Species as Feedstocks for Sustainable Biomaterial Innovation
description: This project asks: What is the viability of using IAS as feedstocks for biomaterials, starting regionally and developing best practices for this approach for global implementation? INVASIFI will provide insights into two environmental challenges: Invasive Alien Species mitigation and new biomaterial development
notes: BID Activity Plan (Dec 2022). Team listado inclui investigadores externos de várias universidades. pensar se vale a pena, nas teams com researchers externos - colocar as suas instituições como external collaborations.

title: Bio-Inspired approaches to computational design (morphogenesis)
description: Bio-inspired algorithms for topology optimization and generative design: development and testing of a set of computational generative algorithms that can be integrated into the creative design process.
